headline: High: caveman’s MCP-backed, multi-instance workflow can amplify prompt injection and cascading errors when paired with a non-runnable docs-only ML resource.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_b explicitly uses MCP and reads files like CLAUDE.md, docs, and project notes, so injected instructions can flow through its inputs. agent_a is a docs-only awesome-list with no runtime surfaces, so the pairwise risk is indirect rather than direct. The interaction is plausible via shared files/manual handoff, but not documented as a shared channel.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests content from files that agent_a helped curate or summarize, injected instructions can propagate.
IF a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge is used between the two, prompt text can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Restrict agent_b to trusted, signed prompt files only.
Add a review step before agent_b consumes any agent_a-generated text.
Keep agent_a outputs in a separate read-only folder.
Disable MCP access for untrusted directories.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches no data classes and has no egress, while agent_b touches token usage, session logs, memory files, and project notes but also has network_egress none. That makes exfiltration unlikely and limits blast radius. The main residual risk is local leakage through shared files or logs, not third-party transmission.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a writable workspace, local file leakage becomes possible.
IF agent_b stores session logs or memory files in a directory readable by agent_a, sensitive notes can be exposed.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories.
Rotate or clear agent_b session logs before sharing workspaces.
Mark memory files read-only for agent_a.
Review project notes for secrets before reuse.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b supports multiple instances and writes to files such as CLAUDE.md, docs, and evals, but agent_a is non-runnable and exposes no write surfaces. Because agent_a cannot act on shared mutable resources, there is no meaningful write-write conflict between the pair. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or manual copying not shown in the profiles.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF agent_a is replaced by a runnable implementation with write permissions, overlap risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize edits to shared files.
Use git branches per agent.
Lock CLAUDE.md during writes.
requires-engineering: add workspace-level mutexes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can consume files and project notes, so if agent_a’s curated content is treated as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream writing or planning. agent_a is a docs-only resource, which makes the pathway indirect, but agent_b’s content-writing role increases the chance of unverified reuse. The pair lacks a built-in verification step in the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a-derived text as source material without verification, factual errors can propagate.
IF agent_b drafts project notes or docs from agent_a summaries, downstream outputs may inherit mistakes.
mitigations: Require source checking before publication.
Keep a citation checklist for agent_b outputs.
Flag agent_a-derived text as untrusted draft material.
Compare claims against primary sources.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or PHI-handling mismatch is evidenced in either profile. agent_a touches no data classes and agent_b lists only operational artifacts like logs and notes, so a compliance breach pathway is not established. The other agent is not cited separately because no cross-border or regulated-data flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into agent_b’s notes or logs, compliance review is required.
IF a deployment policy adds residency constraints not shown here, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in notes or logs.
Review retention settings for session logs.
Keep project notes free of personal data.
Document data-class handling rules.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
